statements.markdown:
[OpenAI (2026a), Lemma 4.1][FS] supplies an explicit polynomial $F_2$
and a decomposition
$$
z^2-12vw^2+6v^4
=\mathcal W(F_2)+\kappa v^4+\mathcal R,
\qquad
\mathcal R\geq0,\qquad
\kappa=\frac{1661507}{1521000000}>\frac1{1000}.
$$

statements.markdown:
Integration removes $\mathcal W(F_2)$ and keeps the fourth-moment
margin, giving
$$
\int_{\mathbb R}(z^2-12vw^2+6v^4)f\,dx
\geq\frac1{1000}\int_{\mathbb R}v^4f\,dx.           \tag{5}
$$

statements.markdown:
At this stage write
$R_c=d^2-12cab^2+6c^2a^4$. The source constructs a correction
$C$ from the spatial derivatives and the density, with

$$
\mathbb E[C(t,X_t)]=0,\qquad
R_c(t,x)+C(t,x)\ge\frac{c^2}{1000}a(t,x)^4.
$$

A rational polynomial identity gives the second inequality by writing
the remainder as a sum of nonnegative terms. The density bounds and vanishing boundary
products justify the first. Consequently

$$
q'''(t)=\mathbb E[R_c(t,X_t)]
=\mathbb E[(R_c+C)(t,X_t)]
\ge\frac{c^2}{1000}\mathbb E[a(t,X_t)^4].
$$
statements.section: 7.3 Where the strict-curvature input comes from
